terms.definition: The reporting interface in this demo. A franchise is a team workspace: choose LA Galaxy for soccer or LA Kings for hockey.
Ticket sales value after cancellations and reversals. It measures sales, not necessarily cash already collected.
Net tickets are tickets remaining after cancellations. Paid tickets have a price; complimentary (comp) tickets are free. Net tickets include both.
Attainment is revenue divided by the target: 80% means $80 of each $100 goal is reached. Gap is target minus revenue; a negative gap means the goal was exceeded.
Pacing shows how sales build over time. Goal pace is the target path toward the final revenue goal. Dana’s chart uses invented paths, not historical performance.
Booked is the synthetic sales recorded so far. The forecast is an invented end result for demonstration, not a prediction from a model. Match-chart “14d” means 14 days before kickoff.
A way to express ticket-plan volume in units of a complete season. Smaller plans can contribute fractions of one FSE; exact counting rules vary. FSE is the plan-sales category in this demo.
Shield’s question-and-answer data assistant. This public demo matches example questions to scripted answers calculated from fake data; it does not call an AI model or a live database.
